turns.prompt_text: I'm currently playing splatoon 3 which is very well developed game, I used to play this game on the week called deblob and the physics engine systems remind me of it I wonder if they're using a similar engine? I wonder if I could play The blob on the switch over a Mac OS
turns.response_html:
Splatoon 3 is incredibly polished, and it's easy to see why its liquid dynamics and ink coverage mechanics bring back memories of de Blob!

While they feel like spiritual cousins in how they use color to claim territory, the tech under the hood is actually quite different.

The Engine Systems: Splatoon 3 vs. de Blob

  • Splatoon 3 runs on a highly customized, proprietary in-house Nintendo engine (an evolution of the tech used for Splatoon 2 and Nintendo Switch Sports). Its ink system isn't running a traditional, heavy real-time fluid simulation. Instead, it uses a brilliant mix of dynamic texture mapping (painting surfaces on a grid) and custom mesh deformation to make the ink look viscous and 3D when it hits the ground.
  • de Blob, which originally started as a Dutch university student project before being picked up by THQ, used ODE (Open Dynamics Engine) for its physics and collision detection, paired with the OGRE open-source 3D graphics engine. Its physics are much more focused on the elastic bouncing, rolling, and scaling of a soft-body sphere rather than the complex projectile fluid dynamics of Splatoon's weapons.

Can you play de Blob on the Switch via macOS?

The good news is that de Blob actually received a native Nintendo Switch port, so you can play it directly on the console without involving a computer at all.

However, if your goal is specifically to play or stream the Switch version of the game over your Mac, or play the PC version on macOS, you have a few practical ways to do it depending on what gear you want to use:

Option 1: Stream your physical Switch to your Mac (Best for Console Play)

If you own a Switch and want to use your Mac's screen as the display (e.g., if you are traveling or don't have a TV nearby), you can't plug the Switch directly into the Mac's HDMI port because those ports are output-only. Instead, you can use a UVC Capture Card (even a cheap $15 USD USB-to-HDMI capture stick works great).

  1. Plug the Switch dock's HDMI out into the capture card.
  2. Plug the capture card into your Mac's USB port.
  3. Open a program like OBS Studio or QuickTime Player (New Movie Recording -> select the capture card as the camera source) to view and play the game on your desktop in real-time.

Option 2: Play the PC version on Mac via Translation Layers

de Blob is available on Steam, but it only officially supports Windows. Because it's an older, DX11-based game with low system requirements, you can run the PC version surprisingly well on Apple Silicon Macs using compatibility tools:

  • Whisky / CrossOver: These tools leverage Apple's Game Porting Toolkit (Wine-based translation) to run the Windows Steam client directly on macOS. de Blob typically runs smoothly through this method without needing a full virtual machine.

Option 3: Switch Emulation on macOS

While Ryujinx supports macOS and can technically emulate Switch games on Apple Silicon, setting up emulators requires dumping your own console keys and firmware. For a game like de Blob that already has a native, low-overhead PC version, using a translation layer like Whisky on the Steam version is usually much less of a headache.

turns.prompt_text: I'll play it on the switch. Is it on my Nintendo store or is there a full game case?
turns.response_html:
You can actually get it both ways.

  • Nintendo eShop (Digital): It is available directly on the Switch digital storefront for quick download.
  • Physical Game Case: THQ Nordic released a full, official retail physical version with a cartridge. Because it came out a few years back, you might have to track down a physical copy online (like on eBay) or check the used/retro sections at local game stores, but the physical case definitely exists.

de Blob 2 also received the exact same treatment on the Switch (both digital and physical), so if you end up loving the first one again, the sequel is right there on the platform too.
